PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS 
Q.	Please state your name and business address.
A.	Adrian Narvaez, Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission), 1701 N. Congress Avenue, Austin, TX 78711-3326.
Q.	By whom are you employed and in what capacity?
A.	I am employed by the Commission as a Rate Analyst in the Tariff and Rate Analysis Section of the Rate Regulation Division.
Q.	What are your responsibilities as a Rate Analyst for the Commission?
A.	My principal responsibility is analyzing utility filings on matters relating to rate design and cost allocation.  My responsibilities include analyzing electric industry regulatory policy, reviewing tariffs to determine compliance with Commission requirements, and preparing and presenting testimony as an expert witness on cost allocation and rate design issues in contested proceedings before the Commission and the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH).
Q.	Please state your educational background and professional experience.
A.	Attachment AN-1 contains a summary of my regulatory experience and educational background.
Q.	Have you previously filed testimony before the Commission?
A.	Yes.  Attachment AN-1 contains a listing of direct testimony I have filed at the Commission.
PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF TESTIMONY
Q.	What is the purpose of your testimony in this proceeding?
A.	My testimony regarding Southwestern Electric Power Company’s (SWEPCO or the Company) application will address, in whole or in part, the following issue from the Commission’s Preliminary Order issued on December 12, 2025:
5.	Should the Commission approve SWEPCO’s proposed tariff?
	c.	Does SWEPCO's proposal adequately address the effects, if any, on SWEPCO's other customers, including residential and small commercial customers?

III.	SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS
Q.	What is your recommendation?
A.	I recommend the Commission require that in all future base rate proceedings, SWEPCO must provide testimony and supporting workpapers demonstrating that costs related to providing service to large load customers, including all generation, transmission and other system upgrades made in order to provide service to SWEPCO’s large load customers, have not been shifted to SWEPCO’s other Texas retail customers.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Q.	What is SWEPCO’s proposal in this docket?
A.	SWEPCO requests Commission approval of a new standard Contract for Electric Service - Large Load (ES-LL Contract). SWEPCO states that its current Contract for Electric Service is not well-suited to address the unique requirements and risks presented by the increase in large load customers that SWEPCO anticipates within its Texas service area. Therefore, approval of a new standard contract for large load customers is needed to provide a standardized framework for these customers while ensuring that existing customers and the Company are not exposed to undue financial risk.
Q.	Is it important to ensure that SWEPCO’s non-large load customers do not bear costs associated with providing service to large load customers?
A.	Yes. The expected increase in data centers and other large load customers presents risks that differ significantly from those associated with traditional customer growth. Serving large-load customers requires substantial investments in generation, transmission, and other system infrastructure long before the utility can realize the revenues associated with those loads. While such investments may be justified when the projected load materializes as expected, there is a risk that a project may be delayed, downsized, or ultimately canceled, leaving the Company with facilities that were constructed to serve a customer that does not ultimately take service at the anticipated level. Without appropriate safeguards, the costs associated with these investments could be shifted to SWEPCO’s other customers.
Q.	Aside from the provisions included in SWEPCO’s proposed ES-LL Contract, do you recommend approval of additional requirements on SWEPCO to ensure that the costs associated with large load customers are not borne by SWEPCO’s other customers? 
A.	Yes. I recommend that in all future base rate proceedings, SWEPCO must provide testimony and supporting workpapers demonstrating that costs related to providing service to large load customers, including all generation, transmission and other system upgrades made in order to provide service to SWEPCO’s large load customers, have not been shifted to SWEPCO’s other Texas retail customers. This requirement will promote transparency and accountability in SWEPCO’s future rate cases and provide the Commission with the information necessary to verify that SWEPCO’s other Texas retail customers are not adversely affected by the Company's efforts to serve large load customers.

CONCLUSION
Q.      	If you do not address an issue or position in your testimony, should that be interpreted as Staff supporting SWEPCO’s position on that issue? 
A.        No.  The fact that I do not address an issue in my testimony should not be construed as agreeing, endorsing, or consenting to any position taken by SWEPCO.
Q. 	Does this conclude your direct testimony?
A. 	Yes.
